CLIENT_ENV.description: Environment identifier and Docker image tag. Canonical values are `dev`, `stg`, `prod`; the documented aliases `development`/`staging`/`production` are accepted and normalized (matching client-runtime proxy_config.ENV_ALIASES). Empty means 'unset' and resolves to prod. THE LIST IS CLOSED (enum above): anything else is rejected at install/upgrade time rather than passed through as a literal image tag. It was open until backend#1723's follow-up, and an out-of-vocabulary value did not degrade -- it silently reconfigured the edge: it became the tag for three control-plane images (no `:prd`/`:qa` tag is published), it missed `images.ingestor.channelTags` so the ingestor fell to the last-resort literal, it missed `serviceDbAccountsByEnv` so no service DB account was provisioned, AND it dropped the prod digest pin, which applies only where the env resolves to exactly `prod`. Load-bearing in four places, validated in none.

RESOURCE_REQUESTS.description: Optional explicit resource requests for spawned training jobs. Comma-separated key=value over a CLOSED set of dimensions: cpu, memory, ephemeral-storage (disk added by backend#2223). Order is free and any subset is allowed; an omitted dimension falls back to jobs-manager's own default. The vocabulary is closed deliberately: client-runtime parses this with a generic key=value split and no allow-list, so a typo such as 'memroy=8Gi' would reach the pod spec as a silently wrong envelope instead of an error. The previous pattern was also leakier than it looked - \S+ matched commas, so 'cpu=2,memory=8Gi,gpu=1' validated. Unset: jobs-manager uses its built-in 'cpu=1,memory=2Gi' literal (the contract floor since backend#2254). The node-allocatable derivation (75%, backend#664 L0) is real but gated OFF behind DERIVE_JOB_ENVELOPE, which is only consulted when BOTH this key and its pair are unset (backend#2167, backend#2250).

RESOURCE_LIMITS.description: Optional explicit resource limits for spawned training jobs. Comma-separated key=value over a CLOSED set of dimensions: cpu, memory, ephemeral-storage (disk added by backend#2223). Order is free and any subset is allowed; an omitted dimension falls back to jobs-manager's own default. The vocabulary is closed deliberately: client-runtime parses this with a generic key=value split and no allow-list, so a typo such as 'memroy=8Gi' would reach the pod spec as a silently wrong envelope instead of an error. The previous pattern was also leakier than it looked - \S+ matched commas, so 'cpu=2,memory=8Gi,gpu=1' validated. Unset: jobs-manager uses its built-in 'cpu=1,memory=2Gi' literal (the contract floor since backend#2254). The node-allocatable derivation (75%, backend#664 L0) is real but gated OFF behind DERIVE_JOB_ENVELOPE, which is only consulted when BOTH this key and its pair are unset (backend#2167, backend#2250).

RESOURCE_PROVENANCE.description: Who chose RESOURCE_REQUESTS/RESOURCE_LIMITS: 'installer' (sized to this machine at install), 'user' (an explicit 'tracebloc resources set'), or 'unknown' (a value carried forward from before this key existed, so provenance is genuinely unknowable). Read-only bookkeeping for backend#2220 - it never changes the envelope, it records who picked it, so a future ladder can re-derive an installer-written value without ever overriding a deliberate human choice.

DERIVE_JOB_ENVELOPE.description: Opt in to the node-derived training-job envelope (backend#664 Utilization Ladder L0): cpu = max(2, floor(allocatable*0.75)), memory = max(8Gi, floor(allocatable*0.75)). WHEN OPTED IN, MEMORY is requests == limits and CPU is a request-only share weight with NO limit since backend#2418, so the job pod is Burstable - not Guaranteed QoS, as this description claimed for both dimensions until backend#2872. With the flag OFF (the default) jobs-manager uses its built-in literal on requests AND limits, so a CPU job pod is Guaranteed. THE CLASS FOLLOWS THE FLAG *AND* WHETHER THE POD REQUESTS A GPU: cpu-only + off -> Guaranteed, cpu-only + on -> Burstable, GPU -> BestEffort either way. A GPU job's envelope resolves to nvidia.com/gpu (and ephemeral-storage) only; neither is QoS-relevant, so the container sets no cpu/memory request or limit at all and the flag changes nothing on that cluster (backend#2871). Do not read 'Burstable' as the default, and do not turn this on expecting to escape Burstable on a GPU node. OFF by default and consulted ONLY when RESOURCE_REQUESTS and RESOURCE_LIMITS are both unset - an explicit envelope always wins, and both installers write that pair unconditionally, so opting an installer-provisioned edge in means clearing both keys too. Turning it on caps the machine at ONE concurrent training job (any Guaranteed fraction >= 50% does), and on an uncapped multi-node k3d cluster every node over-reports the whole Docker VM, so the derivation's min-across-nodes does not protect you (backend#2167). The vocabulary is CLOSED and lowercase: jobs-manager itself lower-cases and strips, so 'True' would also work at runtime, but pinning lowercase here means a typo ('ture') is rejected at install time instead of silently leaving the flag off - the silent-off failure is precisely why backend#2250 exists. Narrowing the accepted set can never make the runtime do something this schema forbade; do not widen it to 'fix' the asymmetry.

GPU_REQUESTS.description: Optional GPU requests for spawned jobs (defaults to 'nvidia.com/gpu=1' if not set) Bounds SCHEDULING, not visibility. Kubernetes uses this to decide how many GPU pods fit on a node -- one at a time at the default -- so concurrent jobs do not contend. It does NOT restrict which devices a container can see when the GPU arrives via CDI: that injection happens outside the Kubernetes resource limit, so on a CDI node (Docker Desktop / WSL2, see GPU_VISIBLE_DEVICES) a pod sees every GPU on the machine regardless of this value. On a device-plugin node the plugin does pin concrete GPU UUIDs, so there the limit is also an isolation boundary -- same key, two meanings, which is why this says so (backend#2657). Setting this to 'nvidia.com/gpu=1' on a multi-GPU CDI box does not cap a job at one device.

GPU_LIMITS.description: Optional GPU limits for spawned jobs (defaults to 'nvidia.com/gpu=1' if not set) Bounds SCHEDULING, not visibility. Kubernetes uses this to decide how many GPU pods fit on a node -- one at a time at the default -- so concurrent jobs do not contend. It does NOT restrict which devices a container can see when the GPU arrives via CDI: that injection happens outside the Kubernetes resource limit, so on a CDI node (Docker Desktop / WSL2, see GPU_VISIBLE_DEVICES) a pod sees every GPU on the machine regardless of this value. On a device-plugin node the plugin does pin concrete GPU UUIDs, so there the limit is also an isolation boundary -- same key, two meanings, which is why this says so (backend#2657). Setting this to 'nvidia.com/gpu=1' on a multi-GPU CDI box does not cap a job at one device.

GPU_VISIBLE_DEVICES.description: Optional CDI device selector threaded into GPU training pods as NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES (client-runtime#291). Set only where the NVIDIA device plugin can't run and the GPU is injected via CDI instead (Docker Desktop / WSL2, where NVML returns ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED — tracebloc/client#616; the Windows installer sets it automatically there). Leave empty on a normal device-plugin node, which owns NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES itself.

SINGLE_NODE.description: Single-node (fixed, non-elastic) cluster flag. Gates jobs-manager's GPU->CPU pending-job fallback (client-runtime#92). 'true' -> downgrade a stuck Pending GPU pod to CPU (correct on fixed single-host clusters where GPU presence is known at install time); 'false' -> leave it for the autoscaler/backend (correct for EKS/AKS/OpenShift). If unset, defaults to hostPath.enabled.

TRACEBLOC_DDP.description: Per-edge OPERATOR switch: DistributedDataParallel across the GPUs a training pod is given. RFC-0067 D8 kill switch / rollback lever (backend#3149; runtime half client-runtime#480). jobs-manager reads it from its own container env and writes an explicit "1" or "0" onto every training pod it spawns. Truthy = 1 | true | yes (case-insensitive, whitespace-tolerant); everything else, including unset, is OFF. THE VOCABULARY IS CLOSED to those spellings plus 0 / false / no (and empty = unset): the runtime treats any unrecognised value as off, so without this a typo such as 'ture' or 'on' would silently disable the very thing the operator believed they had enabled.

TRACEBLOC_AMP.description: Per-edge OPERATOR switch: automatic mixed precision (the engine still picks bf16-vs-fp16 from the device, RFC-0067 D4). RFC-0067 D8 kill switch / rollback lever (backend#3149; runtime half client-runtime#480). jobs-manager reads it from its own container env and writes an explicit "1" or "0" onto every training pod it spawns. Truthy = 1 | true | yes (case-insensitive, whitespace-tolerant); everything else, including unset, is OFF. THE VOCABULARY IS CLOSED to those spellings plus 0 / false / no (and empty = unset): the runtime treats any unrecognised value as off, so without this a typo such as 'ture' or 'on' would silently disable the very thing the operator believed they had enabled.

MULTI_GPU_LEASE_SECONDS.description: Per-run lease for MULTI-GPU runs (RFC-0067 D7/H4; client-runtime#486): applied by jobs-manager as the pod-level activeDeadlineSeconds only when the resolved nvidia.com/gpu limit is above 1, min()'d with the fleet cap. Digits = seconds (jobs-manager defaults to 86400 when unset); 0 / off / false / no disable it. Rendered only when set: the runtime reads an empty value as DISABLED, so an unconditional chart default would switch the lease off fleet-wide. THE VOCABULARY IS CLOSED because the runtime falls back to its default on anything unrecognised, which would make a typo indistinguishable from the default.

enabled.description: Render a Helm-managed GPU device-plugin DaemonSet.

vendor.description: Which vendor plugin to render when enabled; required non-empty when enabled is true.

namespace.description: Namespace for the DaemonSet (kube-system by default).

resources.description: Device-plugin pod resources. ONE cpu/memory pair, applied to BOTH requests and limits, because the pod must be Guaranteed QoS (backend#2871): if it is OOM-killed the node stops advertising its GPU resource and every GPU training pod on it goes Pending. A separate requests/limits shape is deliberately NOT expressible here — that is how Guaranteed gets lost by accident. system-node-critical does not cover this; it ranks preemption, not the kernel's oom_score_adj.

cpu.description: cpu for both requests and limits (Kubernetes quantity).

memory.description: memory for both requests and limits (Kubernetes quantity).

resources.description: Device-plugin pod resources. ONE cpu/memory pair, applied to BOTH requests and limits, because the pod must be Guaranteed QoS (backend#2871): if it is OOM-killed the node stops advertising its GPU resource and every GPU training pod on it goes Pending. A separate requests/limits shape is deliberately NOT expressible here — that is how Guaranteed gets lost by accident. system-node-critical does not cover this; it ranks preemption, not the kernel's oom_score_adj.

cpu.description: cpu for both requests and limits (Kubernetes quantity).

memory.description: memory for both requests and limits (Kubernetes quantity).

create.description: Set to false to use an existing StorageClass

provisioner.description: CSI provisioner (required when create is true)

enabled.description: Enable hostPath PVs (bare-metal only). PV paths are fixed: /tracebloc/data, /tracebloc/logs, /tracebloc/mysql. Directories are created via hostPath type: DirectoryOrCreate.

datasetPath.description: Base host path for the DATASET (shared-images) PV ONLY. Default /tracebloc keeps datasets local alongside mysql/logs; the installer sets /tracebloc-data when a customer network (NFS) dataset mount is provided via HOST_DATASET_DIR (backend#743). mysql + logs PV paths always stay on /tracebloc. The chart appends /<release>/data.

singleNode.description: Cluster topology: does this cluster have a single schedulable node? Gates the AUTO-mode single-replica PodDisruptionBudgets (a minAvailable:1 PDB is undrainable on one node). null => default to hostPath.enabled; true/false => explicit. Deliberately separate from env.SINGLE_NODE (GPU->CPU fallback, which may be true on a fixed multi-node cluster). The installer sets true for node-local single-node k3d (client#560).

data.description: Storage size for shared data PVC

clusterScope.description: Use ClusterRole (true) or namespace-scoped Role (false). Defaults to true.

resourceMonitor.description: Deploy resource-monitor DaemonSet. Defaults to true.

nodeAgents.description: Dedicated namespace for node-level agents (resource-monitor). Isolates hostPath-using DaemonSets from the restricted release namespace.

create.description: When true, the chart templates the node-agents Namespace with privileged PSA labels. Set false when the namespace is managed out-of-band.

name.description: Name of the namespace that hosts node-level agents. Must exist before install if create is false.

namespace.description: Optional chart-managed Namespace resource with Pod Security Admission labels

create.description: When true, the chart templates a Namespace with PSA labels and helm.sh/resource-policy: keep. Only use on greenfield installs.

podSecurity.description: Pod Security Admission labels. Enforce is OFF by default; mysql init + resource-monitor currently violate restricted.

networkPolicy.description: NetworkPolicy egress lockdown for untrusted training pods. Requires a CNI that enforces NetworkPolicy.

enabled.description: Create the training-egress NetworkPolicy. Set false on clusters without an enforcing CNI.

allowExternalHttps.description: When false (the default, RFC-0003 D6), drop the 0.0.0.0/0:443 egress rule so training pods reach only DNS, MySQL, requests-proxy and the egress gateway (SECURITY §8.2 / client-runtime#102). Set true to opt a fleet back out to direct egress. An absent key on a `--reuse-values` upgrade from a release predating it keeps the old permissive behaviour.

enforcementProbeHost.description: Host the `helm test` enforcement check curls directly (when allowExternalHttps=false) to verify the CNI blocks egress; non-enforcement fails the test (a test hook never affects install/upgrade) — client-runtime#104. Empty string disables it (e.g. air-gapped clusters).

enforcementProbeTimeoutSeconds.description: Max seconds the egress-enforcement `helm test` waits for egress to become blocked before failing. Covers standard-mode CNI reconciliation (e.g. AWS VPC CNI NETWORK_POLICY_ENFORCING_MODE=standard). 60s suits AWS VPC CNI / Calico / Cilium; raise on slow nodes.

dnsNamespace.description: Namespace where the cluster DNS service runs

dnsSelector.description: Pod labels selecting the cluster DNS service. AKS/EKS/kubeadm: {k8s-app: kube-dns}. OpenShift: {dns.operator.openshift.io/daemonset-dns: default}

clusterCidrs.description: In-cluster pod+service CIDRs to block pod-to-pod egress on port 443. Override to match your cluster CIDRs. Must be non-empty when networkPolicy.training.enabled is true — an empty list renders `except: null` and Kubernetes treats that as no exceptions, silently allowing unrestricted in-cluster egress.

egressReachabilityCheck.description: Backend-reachability seal check (helm test hook). Set enabled=false only on truly air-gapped clusters with no route to the backend.

enabled.description: Render the backend-reachability helm test hook Job. A test hook never affects install/upgrade.

perExperimentDbCreds.description: OPERATOR OVERRIDE, normally unset. When null the effective value comes from perExperimentDbCredsByEnv keyed on the RESOLVED CLIENT_ENV. RFC-0003 D10 (backend#1181): mint a per-experiment MySQL user scoped to the experiment's own table(s), injected via a per-job Secret, instead of the shared edgeuser. Set true or false only to pin ONE edge against its fleet default.

perExperimentDbCredsByEnv.description: Per-environment default for the RFC-0003 D10 per-experiment credential mint (backend#1528), keyed on the RESOLVED CLIENT_ENV (dev|stg|prod; documented aliases normalize first). Every other gate in this rollout had one of these; without it, the flag the ticket's LAST step is gated on was the only one whose fleet posture the chart could not record — so a values-resetting upgrade silently put the account mint back on edgeuser.

narrowEdgeuser.description: OPERATOR OVERRIDE, normally unset. When null the effective value comes from narrowEdgeuserByEnv keyed on the resolved CLIENT_ENV. backend#1528 S3 close-out: REVOKE the root-equivalent edgeuser to USAGE only at every jobs-manager boot, so a fleet that completed the retirement STAYS retired. mysql-client-initdb/10-edgeuser-bridge-grants.sql re-grants edgeuser its broad privileges at every FRESH datadir init and cannot branch on a runtime flag — it is baked into a digest-frozen image and the mysql entrypoint runs it before jobs-manager exists — so without this a reinstall or a datadir loss silently hands the fleet a root-equivalent account again. It REVOKEs, never DROPs: the account keeps existing with USAGE only, reversible from the S0 SHOW GRANTS snapshot, and DROP USER stays an operator step. ONLY LEGAL WITH ALL THREE PREDECESSORS ON (bootstrapDbReparent, serviceDbAccounts, perExperimentDbCreds), and that pairing is ENFORCED rather than documented — the render FAILS on a mis-paired combination and jobs-manager refuses it again at startup. Verify a fleet with docs/migration-tools/edgeuser-drop-readiness.sh before flipping it.

narrowEdgeuserByEnv.description: Per-environment default for narrowEdgeuser, keyed on the RESOLVED CLIENT_ENV (documented aliases normalize first). TRUE for dev, false for stg and prod: this is the last step of backend#1528's last stage, so a fleet opts in only once its posture is verified -- dev's is, so a fresh dev install comes up already retired. Flipping it where any predecessor gate is off fails the render — see narrowEdgeuser.

credmgrPassword.description: RFC-0003 D10 (backend#1181): optional operator pin for the tb_credmgr account password (3-tier resolution, mirrors podTokenSigningSecret). Empty = generate-and-persist. Set for DR / a pre-created MySQL account / forced rotation, or to keep it stable across a perExperimentDbCreds toggle. Must be alphanumeric.

serviceDbAccounts.description: OPERATOR OVERRIDE, normally unset. When null the effective value comes from serviceDbAccountsByEnv keyed on the resolved CLIENT_ENV (backend#1752). Set true/false to force one answer on this edge regardless of environment. backend#1528 S1 (RFC-0003 D10 close-out): provision the dedicated MySQL service identities tb_meta (metadata DB) and tb_ingest (dataset DB) that replace the root-equivalent edgeuser. S2 has shipped, so wherever this is on the consumers authenticate as the dedicated identities; only an explicit override-off renders the shared-edgeuser path byte-for-byte. Flip per environment, dev first.

tbMetaPassword.description: backend#1528 S1: optional operator pin for the tb_meta account password (3-tier resolution, mirrors credmgrPassword). Empty = generate-and-persist. Set for DR / a pre-created MySQL account / forced rotation. Must be alphanumeric.

tbIngestPassword.description: backend#1528 S1: optional operator pin for the tb_ingest account password (3-tier resolution, mirrors credmgrPassword). Empty = generate-and-persist. Set for DR / a pre-created MySQL account / forced rotation. Must be alphanumeric.

bootstrapDbReparent.description: OPERATOR OVERRIDE, normally unset. When null the effective value comes from bootstrapDbReparentByEnv keyed on the resolved CLIENT_ENV, mirroring serviceDbAccounts. backend#1528 S3 (RFC-0003 D10 close-out, FINAL stage): re-parent the account-minting bootstrap DDL off the root-equivalent edgeuser onto MySQL root (client-runtime#310 reads DB_BOOTSTRAP_USER/PASSWORD), the prerequisite for REVOKE/DROP of edgeuser. Off everywhere by default; flip per environment dev-first, only after serviceDbAccounts + perExperimentDbCreds are verified on the fleet and the S0 SHOW GRANTS snapshot is captured. When on, bootstrapDbPassword is REQUIRED.

bootstrapDbPassword.description: backend#1528 S3: REQUIRED when bootstrapDbReparent resolves on — the password jobs-manager authenticates with as MySQL root to run the mint DDL. NO generated default (2-tier: operator pin -> existing Secret value -> Helm fails): jobs-manager authenticates as root and never runs ALTER USER root, so a random value would lock the minter out and CrashLoop it. Set to the mysql-client image's baked root password (see backend#947 for the value and its rotated replacement). NOT constrained to alphanumeric — never interpolated into DDL, only a connection parameter.

rotateMysqlRoot.description: OPERATOR OVERRIDE, normally unset. When null the effective value comes from rotateMysqlRootByEnv keyed on the resolved CLIENT_ENV, mirroring serviceDbAccounts. backend#947 / backend#1528 Phase 0: chart-manage the mysql-client root password (generated Secret + MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD env) so a FRESH datadir is born rotated off the image's baked literal. Off everywhere by default. Only rotates a fresh datadir; an existing edge needs the one-time ALTER USER 'root' rollout DDL (reads the same Secret). Turning it on rolls the mysql pod.

mysqlRootPassword.description: backend#947: optional operator pin for the mysql-client root password (3-tier resolution, mirrors credmgrPassword). Empty = generate-and-persist when rotateMysqlRoot is on. Set for DR or to match a root account rotated out-of-band. Must be alphanumeric ([A-Za-z0-9]+) — the rotation runbook embeds it in an ALTER USER ... IDENTIFIED BY '...' statement, so metacharacters would break the one-time rotation (generated randAlphaNum already satisfies this). Constrained where bootstrapDbPassword is not: that is only a connection parameter, this also lands in DDL.

mysqlRootRotationAcknowledged.description: backend#2879: acknowledge the manual root-rotation migration on an EXISTING fleet. Normally unset. When rotateMysqlRoot resolves on and the chart would MINT (no mysqlRootPassword pin, no MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD in the live Secret), the render FAILS at template time naming docs/migration-tools/rotate-mysql-root.md unless this is true — because the mysql entrypoint honours MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD only at fresh-datadir init, so root would otherwise authenticate with neither value (helm reports success; jobs-manager CrashLoops on 1045). It clears ALL of the guard's refuse arms: the datadir PVC exists (lookup), mysqlDatadirExists is declared, or (backend#2892, fail-closed) the render cannot see a cluster at all. Set true ONLY as part of that runbook: it asserts you will run the one-time ALTER USER 'root' DDL in the same window; it runs no DDL itself. Self-expiring ONLY on a live/server-side render — once rotated, tier 2 (a live lookup of the Secret) preserves the value and the mint is never reached again. On a CLUSTER-LESS render tier 2 is empty every render, so it does NOT self-expire there: rotating a cluster-less fleet on the ack alone leaves it permanently set and permanently disarms the guard (and it replays through --reuse-values / --reset-then-reuse-values), so pin mysqlRootPassword or render server-side instead. A FRESH install on a live cluster never needs it.

mysqlDatadirExists.description: backend#2892 (chart >= 1.9.90): declare that this fleet's MySQL datadir ALREADY EXISTS. Normally unset — the fail-closed root-rotation guard already covers most fleets: a cluster-less render REFUSES the mint by default (it cannot see a cluster), and a live render DETECTS the datadir by its PVC lookup. This is the explicit assertion for the gaps those leave: a LIVE render whose datadir PVC the lookup cannot see (a renamed or not-yet-bound PVC), and message clarity (with it set, the refusal names the existing-datadir migration specifically rather than the generic cannot-see-a-cluster message). Pin it in the fleet's checked-in overlay: a durable per-fleet fact. PROTECTION, not a rotation path — like the acknowledgement it does not make a cluster-less rotation converge (the minted value is not preserved offline: tier-2 preservation is a live lookup too, the clientId/clientPassword limit), so to actually rotate a cluster-less fleet pin mysqlRootPassword (tier 1, stable, and it bypasses the mint) or render server-side. A FRESH install leaves it unset; charts < 1.9.90 ignore it (open schema). See docs/migration-tools/rotate-mysql-root.md.

perIngestionTables.description: RFC-0003 D16 (backend#1204/#1205): stamp PER_INGESTION_TABLES=1 into every ingestion Job. Flip per environment, dev first; file-bearing categories are refused under the flag until client-runtime#203 phase 2.

perDatasetPvcs.description: RFC-0003 D9 Track B (client-runtime#203/#261): stamp PER_DATASET_PVCS=1 into jobs-manager — training pods get one read-only hostPath PV/PVC per dataset handle instead of a subPath view of the shared PVC. Single-node/hostPath clusters only; requires clusterScope (PVs are cluster-scoped).

ingestionAuthz.description: Authorization policy for POST /internal/submit-ingestion-run on jobs-manager (client-runtime#21). Rendered into the ingestion-authz ConfigMap.

serviceAccountName.description: Name of the shared ServiceAccount this chart creates for ingestor subchart releases (client#129). Single source of truth for the SA template and the default `allowed` entry.

allowed.description: Maps (namespace, service_account) to permitted table-name prefixes. Empty renders `allowed: []` (deny-all, fail-safe).

service_account.description: SA name. Omit to fall back to ingestionAuthz.serviceAccountName.

namespace.description: SA namespace. Omit to fall back to the release namespace.

table_prefixes.description: Table-name prefixes this SA may ingest into. ["*"] = any table.

podTokenSigningSecret.description: HMAC secret for signing pod-proxy tokens. Empty (default) auto-generates a stable secret on first install and reuses it via lookup on upgrade. Set explicitly only to pin or rotate (rotating invalidates all live tokens).

podTokenTtlSeconds.description: Backstop lifetime (seconds) for a signed pod-proxy token. Set to comfortably exceed the longest expected training-job duration or long-running jobs 401 mid-run. Default 7 days.

sealCheck.description: Seal check — the chart's conformance suite (RFC-0003 §8.2 / backend#1184). Every check is a `helm test` hook Job labelled tracebloc.io/seal-check=true + tracebloc.io/seal-check-name=<check> (the enumeration contract the tracebloc CLI consumes, cli#393). See docs/SEAL-CHECK.md.

storageAssertions.description: In-cluster storage assertions: release PVCs Bound on the expected StorageClass; in dynamic-PVC mode (hostPath.enabled=false) no release PVC backed by a hostPath PV on an unmanaged host tree (leftover chart hostPath PVs capture claims via claimRef — RFC-0003 D3/D4).

enabled.description: Render the storage-assertions `helm test` hook Job (plus its least-privilege SA/RBAC test hooks).

timeoutSeconds.description: Max seconds to wait for all release PVCs to reach Bound before failing (covers WaitForFirstConsumer classes and first-install image pulls).

nodeLocalPathPrefixes.description: hostPath prefixes accepted as provisioner-managed node-local storage in dynamic mode (k3s local-path: /var/lib/rancher/…; upstream local-path-provisioner: /opt/local-path-provisioner/). Entries match whole path segments (trailing slash optional) — a prefix admits itself and paths under it, never sibling paths. Any other hostPath backing fails the check.

image.description: kubectl-capable image for the assertion pod (same image the image-refresh CronJob uses).

egressProxy.description: In-cluster squid egress gateway (SECURITY §8.2 / client-runtime#102). Forward proxy that permits HTTPS CONNECT only to the allowlist, so a locked-down training pod can reach the backend + App Insights and nothing else.

routeWorkloads.description: Route training-pod outbound HTTPS through the gateway (jobs-manager injects HTTPS_PROXY). Default true (RFC-0003 D6, deny-by-default); set false to opt a fleet out of gateway routing.

allowlist.description: FQDNs the gateway permits HTTPS CONNECT to (squid dstdomain syntax: leading dot = subdomain match, bare host = exact).

images.description: Container image pinning. Prefer digest over tag for immutability.

digest.description: Optional image digest (sha256:...). When set, overrides the tag, opts this image out of image-refresh, and is ALSO inherited by the requests-proxy Deployment, which runs the same image (see images.requestsProxy.digest).
Optional image digest (sha256:...). When set, overrides the tag and opts this image out of image-refresh.

Optional image digest (sha256:...). When set, overrides the tag and opts the resource-monitor DaemonSet out of image-refresh (#569 brought it under refresh; before that it had no deliberate update path at all).

Optional image digest (sha256:...) for the requests-proxy Deployment, which runs the tracebloc/jobs-manager image. Leave EMPTY (default) and it follows images.jobsManager.digest, so the two pods cannot run different builds of the same image. Set it only to pin requests-proxy independently of jobs-manager.

ingestor.description: Image used for spawned ingestion Jobs. jobs-manager resolves one effective digest from these keys (see the tracebloc.ingestorDigest helper) and builds the reference from it (client-runtime submit_ingestion_run): digest set -> repo@digest + IfNotPresent, digest empty -> repo:tag + Always. Prod pins `prodDigest` (a chart default, so a republished pin propagates through the fleet auto-upgrade — backend#1245); dev/staging float on `tag`, resolving the current published digest at every spawn.

repository.description: Ingestor image repository. Override for a private mirror / air-gapped registry (must host the same tag/digest). Surfaces into jobs-manager as INGESTOR_IMAGE_REPOSITORY. Default ghcr.io/tracebloc/ingestor.

tag.description: Explicit floating-tag override for the spawned ingestor. EMPTY by default: the effective tag then comes from channelTags[CLIENT_ENV] (backend#1360). `latest` is rejected — spawn behaviour must not drift. To pin an exact image prefer `digest`, which wins over any tag. Surfaces as INGESTOR_IMAGE_TAG.

channelTags.description: Per-environment floating tags, keyed on the resolved CLIENT_ENV, used when `tag` is empty. `dev`/`stg` track the UNSIGNED internal channels published from the matching data-ingestors branch; `prod` stays a semver float because no :prod tag is published. backend#1360. KEYS ARE CLOSED (`additionalProperties: false`): the lookup is on the RESOLVED env, so only `dev`/`stg`/`prod` can ever match. Before this, `channelTags.staging: "0.8.2"` on a staging edge validated fine and was then ignored -- CLIENT_ENV=staging normalizes to `stg` and read `channelTags.stg` -- so the same word was normalized one key over and meaningless here. Write the canonical key even when you wrote the alias in CLIENT_ENV.

dev.description: Tag spawned when CLIENT_ENV resolves to dev.

stg.description: Tag spawned when CLIENT_ENV resolves to stg.

prod.description: Tag spawned when CLIENT_ENV resolves to prod and no digest applies.

prodDigest.description: Prod reproducibility pin (sha256:<64 hex>), applied when `prodPin` resolves true (i.e. CLIENT_ENV resolves to prod). A CHART DEFAULT by design: `helm upgrade --reset-then-reuse-values` (the fleet auto-upgrade) adopts new chart defaults but re-applies stored user-supplied values, so only a default can update an installed edge (backend#1245). Must be a multi-arch index (#186); regenerate with scripts/resolve-ingestor-digest.sh --write and bump Chart.yaml.

prodPin.description: Whether `prodDigest` applies on this edge. Default true = pin on prod only; dev/staging carry env.CLIENT_ENV=dev|stg and keep floating on `tag`. Set false on a canary prod edge to float it while the rest of the fleet stays pinned.

ackDrift.description: Acknowledged, expected drift for THIS pin (backend#2673). Present only when `prodDigest` is deliberately held behind the `channelTags.prod` float (docs/SECURITY.md §4.1.1). scripts/check-digest-drift.sh then treats the float resolving away from the pin as EXPECTED (job green, printed ACKNOWLEDGED) instead of a finding -- while still re-verifying the pin itself resolves to a healthy multi-arch index, and while ANY OTHER pin drifting still reds. Not consumed by any template; a CI/watch declaration that lives next to the pin and behind CODEOWNERS review. Acknowledge the CLASS, never a specific float digest. Remove this block in the same change that advances the pin off the boundary.

line.description: The channel line the acknowledgement was reasoned about. MUST equal channelTags.prod; if the prod float is moved to a new line these stop matching, the acknowledgement lapses, and the watch reds until the boundary is re-derived for the new line and both are updated.

reason.description: Human justification for holding the pin behind its float, surfaced verbatim in the ACKNOWLEDGED report. State WHY, so a reader sees when it no longer applies.

digest.description: Optional explicit per-edge pin (sha256:<64 hex>). Empty (default) = let prodPin/CLIENT_ENV decide. When set it wins over `prodDigest` and over `prodPin: false` in ANY environment, and every ingestion Job runs this exact image with imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent (reproducibility). Must be a multi-arch index (#186). Surfaces as INGESTOR_IMAGE_DIGEST.

tag.description: Image tag for mysql-client. Empty falls back to the literal `prod` in EVERY environment -- NOT to env.CLIENT_ENV, which is what this said until backend#1723's follow-up. The template is `.Values.images.mysqlClient.tag | default "prod"`, and dev/stg/prod edges all render `mysql-client:prod`. The doc was not merely imprecise, it was an instruction to break the edge: tracebloc/mysql-client publishes 8.0, 8.4, four 8.4-<sha> builds, latest and prod -- there is no `dev` or `stg` tag -- so a reader who believed it and set an env-derived tag would pull a nonexistent image AND disarm the mysql-format-guard, since tracebloc.mysqlEngineMajor maps an unrecognized tag to "unknown" and the guard stands down. Must not be "latest".

resources.description: Container resource requests and limits for mysql, jobs-manager, and pods-monitor. See values.yaml for the rationale behind the defaults.

limits.description: CPU limit deliberately omitted in defaults — throttling causes InnoDB lock-wait timeouts.

priorityClass.description: Cluster-scoped PriorityClass for tracebloc data-plane workloads (mysql). An empty `name` disables the priorityClassName reference on the mysql pod entirely (mysql falls back to default priority 0 — only set this if you explicitly want no OOM protection from the scheduler).

allOf.$comment: If we are templating the PriorityClass resource, name must not be empty. `required: [create]` is needed because draft-07 `properties` only validates keys that are present — without it, omitting `create` passes the `if` vacuously and unconditionally enforces `then`. Same pattern as dockerRegistry below.

create.description: null (default) = auto: render on multi-node CSI (hostPath.enabled=false), skip on single-node/bare-metal (hostPath.enabled=true). true = force render, false = never render. See tracebloc/client#560.
null (default) = auto: render on multi-node CSI (hostPath.enabled=false), skip on single-node/bare-metal (hostPath.enabled=true). true = force render, false = never render. See tracebloc/client#560.

clientId.description: Client ID for authentication. Issued by the backend. May be left empty when the release Secret already carries a CLIENT_ID key -- templates/secrets.yaml resolves values first, then the existing Secret, then fails (backend#2571). `minLength` and the top-level `required` entry were removed for exactly that reason: schema validation runs BEFORE rendering, so either one made the Secret path unreachable. A genuinely missing credential is still refused, by the template, which is the only layer that can see the Secret. Placeholders are still rejected here.

clientPassword.description: Client authentication password. Issued by the backend. May be left empty when the release Secret already carries a CLIENT_PASSWORD key -- see clientId above for why `minLength` and `required` were removed. Prefer pre-creating the Secret: a value passed here is stored in the Helm release's user-supplied values in cleartext, in every retained revision.

autoUpgrade.description: Self-upgrade CronJob (issue tracebloc/client#69). Polls the helm repo at autoUpgrade.repoUrl daily and runs `helm upgrade --reuse-values` when a newer chart version is published. Disable to keep the release pinned to its install-time chart version.

enabled.description: When false, no CronJob, ServiceAccount, or ClusterRoleBinding is rendered and the release will not self-upgrade.

schedule.description: Cron expression in the controller's timezone (UTC unless the cluster overrides it).

repoUrl.description: Helm chart repository URL polled for newer versions.

repoName.description: Local alias used by `helm repo add` inside the upgrade Pod.

chartName.description: Chart name as published in the repo's index.yaml (the `name` field, not the directory).

timeout.description: Passed to `helm upgrade --timeout`. Allow enough headroom for image pull + PVC bind on slow infra.

pendingWedgeMinAge.description: How long a release must sit in pending-upgrade/pending-rollback before the hourly recovery treats it as an abandoned wedge (rolls it back) rather than an in-flight upgrade (leaves it alone) — tracebloc/client#2877. Keep it above the longest hand-run upgrade and below the schedule gap. Default 45m.

suspend.description: CronJob.spec.suspend. Set true to pause without removing the resources.

tag.description: Pin the helm version. `latest` is rejected — auto-upgrade behaviour must not drift.

imageRefresh.description: Image-refresh CronJob (issue tracebloc/client#154; reworked by #569). Polls Docker Hub for the jobs-manager, pods-monitor and resource-monitor digests under the floating CLIENT_ENV tag and, on a change, pins the new digest onto the running workloads with `kubectl set image` (jobs-manager + requests-proxy Deployments and the resource-monitor DaemonSet). It used to `kubectl rollout restart` a single Deployment; the reference change is what lets those pods run imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent and survive an offline restart. Disable to keep the running image in place until manual restart — the chart then renders imagePullPolicy=Always on the unpinned control-plane images, because a floating tag plus a restart is the only update path left.

enabled.description: When false, no CronJob, ServiceAccount, Role, or RoleBinding is rendered. The control-plane workloads will not auto-refresh on new image pushes, and the unpinned ones fall back to imagePullPolicy=Always so a manual restart still picks up a new build (see tracebloc.controlPlanePullPolicy).

schedule.description: Cron expression. Keep the tick rate compatible with Docker Hub's 100/6h anonymous pull-rate limit. Since #569 each tick HEADs THREE manifests (jobs-manager, pods-monitor, resource-monitor), not two — at the default 15m that is 12/hr, i.e. 72 per 6h. Widen the schedule on edges that share an egress IP with other Docker Hub consumers; a digest pin removes that image's HEAD from every tick.

rolloutTimeout.description: Passed to `kubectl rollout status --timeout`. Allow headroom for bare-metal image pull.

activeDeadlineSeconds.description: CronJob jobTemplate.spec.activeDeadlineSeconds. MUST exceed 3 x rolloutTimeout: since #569 a tick re-images jobs-manager, requests-proxy and the resource-monitor DaemonSet in sequence, waiting on each. Blowing the deadline kills the Job mid-wait, so the digest annotation never advances and the shared refresh-attempt counter trips the flap lockout for every control-plane image at once.

maxRefreshAttempts.description: Consecutive failed rollout attempts (same target digest) after which the refresh backs off instead of re-imaging a flapping workload every tick (#563). The counter is shared across all reconciled workloads.

suspend.description: CronJob.spec.suspend. Set true to pause without removing the resources.

tag.description: Pin the alpine/k8s version. `latest` is rejected — image-refresh behaviour must not drift.

dockerRegistry.description: Optional. Omit entirely or set null for public images (no secret or imagePullSecrets). Either create: true with the credentials below, or existingSecret naming a Secret you made yourself -- never both.

create.description: When true, create registry secret and add imagePullSecrets to workloads. Omit dockerRegistry or set false for public images.

existingSecret.description: Name of a kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson Secret you created yourself. Mutually exclusive with create: the chart references this Secret and never writes it, because it has no credentials to write it with. You must create it in every namespace that pulls -- the release namespace, plus nodeAgents.namespace.name while resourceMonitor is true, plus gpu.devicePlugin.namespace while that is enabled -- since the chart cannot mirror a Secret whose contents it does not have.

serviceDbAccountsByEnv.description: Per-environment default for the dedicated tb_meta/tb_ingest identities, keyed on the RESOLVED CLIENT_ENV (dev|stg|prod — documented aliases are normalized first). This is the mechanism behind #1151's 'flip per environment, dev first'; before it, that plan had no implementation and the fleet's posture could not be read in one place. backend#1752.

bootstrapDbReparentByEnv.description: Per-environment default for the backend#1528 S3 bootstrap re-parent (edgeuser -> root for the account-minting DDL), keyed on the RESOLVED CLIENT_ENV (dev|stg|prod — aliases normalized first). Mirrors serviceDbAccountsByEnv. This is the LAST, edgeuser-retiring step. Baked ON for dev, stg and prod, but on the baked path it re-parents ONLY a fresh or already-rotated edge (see rotateMysqlRoot / backend#947) so an existing un-rotated edge is left alone rather than wedged; an accessible existing edge is rotated by the explicit override plus the one-time ALTER USER 'root'.

rotateMysqlRootByEnv.description: Per-environment default for the backend#947 mysql-client root-password rotation, keyed on the RESOLVED CLIENT_ENV (dev|stg|prod — aliases normalized first). Baked ON for dev, stg and prod, but the baked default rotates ONLY a fresh datadir on a live cluster (born rotated) or an already-rotated edge (preserved); an existing un-rotated / blind edge falls back to its current password rather than wedging (tracebloc.bakedRootRotationOn, backend#947). An accessible existing edge is rotated by the explicit override plus the one-time ALTER USER 'root' DDL.

fullnameOverride.description: Rename the resources this chart creates without uninstall + reinstall (backend#2626). Unset resolves to .Release.Name verbatim, so leaving it alone is byte-identical to before it existed. Renames RESOURCES, not the Helm release: app.kubernetes.io/instance, meta.helm.sh/release-name and the RELEASE_NAME env keep the release name, and release-scoped on-disk paths keep it too because a path is a location, not a name. Changing it on an existing install is a migration (Helm renames as delete + create), not a config tweak. THE PATTERN AND LENGTH ARE THE ONES HELM ENFORCES ON THE VALUE THIS REPLACES: a release name is a DNS-1123 label capped at 53 characters, so without them this key was a strictly weaker gate than the thing it substitutes for. A value like Bad_Name! templated clean and then failed object-by-object at the API server, mid-install, leaving a partly-created release. Declared here so it fails at template time, by name (reviewer, backend#2626). THE EMPTY STRING IS ACCEPTED EXPLICITLY: the template treats it as unset (default .Release.Name .Values.fullnameOverride) and values.yaml ships `fullnameOverride: ""` as its commented example, so a pattern requiring at least one character would reject the chart's own documented line if uncommented verbatim (Arturo). CHANGING IT ON A LIVE RELEASE IS REFUSED at template time by secrets.yaml, not merely discouraged - earlier prose here called it a migration, which invited planning one the chart will not start.

telemetryCollector.description: Edge telemetry Collector (RFC-BACKEND-1872 D6/D7, backend#1906). An OpenTelemetry Collector DaemonSet reading Class A container stdout and forwarding to the backend's ingest endpoint. Ships DISABLED: its exporter authenticates with a Secret jobs-manager writes (backend#2274), and enabling it first spools to every node's disk with nothing to deliver. `type` allows null so `--reuse-values` from a release predating this block validates.

enabled.description: Tri-state, and its ABSENCE is meaningful (backend#1906). true = an operator opted in, and a missing token Secret refuses the release. false = an operator opted out. Absent = nobody chose, so the chart collects where the token Secret is present and otherwise SKIPS, recording why in the <release>-telemetry-status ConfigMap rather than failing an unattended auto-upgrade. NO `default` HERE ON PURPOSE: a default would make the absent case unreachable, and the absent case is the whole mechanism.

tag.description: Must be >= 0.130: `block_on_overflow` and `sizer: bytes` on a persistent queue do not exist below it, and the Collector rejects unknown config keys rather than ignoring them.

classAContainers.description: CONTAINER names (not workload names) in the RELEASE namespace whose stdout is collected. Class A per D12. Verified against the rendered chart by scripts/tests/collector-class-a-agreement.sh.

classANodeAgentContainers.description: Class A containers in nodeAgents.namespace rather than the release namespace — the namespace is part of the filelog path.

authScheme.description: `Token` for the edge's DRF user token, which the ingest endpoint accepts via TokenAuthentication. `Bearer` is the ClientAccessToken type and 401s silently — a CLOSED set so a typo cannot pick a third.

blockOnOverflow.description: false = drop-newest, per D7's 2026-08-20 amendment. true stalls the pipeline and relocates loss to kubelet rotation, uncounted.

retryMaxElapsedTime.description: 0 = retry forever, so the byte cap is the ONLY bound. Any positive value silently overrides it.
